sources.title: Statement by the Monetary Policy Board: Monetary Policy Decision
Financial Stability Review October 2026: The Global Macro-financial Environment
Financial Stability Review October 2026: Resilience of Australian Households and Businesses
ASX markets and business live updates, 1 October 2026

observation_candidates.proposition: Middle East conflict and oil-supply disruption are maintaining materially higher global energy prices and adding to Australian inflation pressure.
counter_evidence: Supply-chain adaptation and inventories have absorbed part of recent disruption; duration remains unresolved.
observation_candidates.notes: Candidate observation only; it does not establish the full downstream transmission path.

observation_candidates.proposition: Global sovereign-bond vulnerabilities and higher yields can tighten Australian financing conditions through international financial-market spillovers.
counter_evidence: Major markets remain orderly; a severe Australian funding spillover is not established here.
observation_candidates.notes: Global exposure candidate; no domestic-yield attribution is asserted.

observation_candidates.proposition: The RBA raised the cash-rate target by 25 basis points to 4.60 per cent on 29 September 2026 and retained the option of further tightening if needed.
counter_evidence: Output growth has slowed and policy remains data-dependent.
observation_candidates.notes: Observed policy state, not a forecast.

observation_candidates.proposition: The RBA reports housing prices have fallen in most capital cities and new housing loans have declined noticeably.
counter_evidence: Falling prices alone do not establish forced selling or systemic balance-sheet stress.
observation_candidates.notes: Secondary Cotality monthly figures remain discovery context until separately governed.

observation_candidates.proposition: The RBA estimates around 2 per cent of variable-rate owner-occupier borrowers have insufficient income to cover scheduled mortgage payments and essential expenses.
counter_evidence: The affected share remains small in aggregate and arrears remain low.
observation_candidates.notes: Supports early Stage 2 compression, not systemic default.

observation_candidates.proposition: Current Stage 3 evidence is limited: arrears remain low, less than 1 per cent of borrowers are in negative equity, and the median mortgagor can cover over a year of scheduled payments from offset/redraw buffers.
counter_evidence: Buffers are uneven and could weaken if labour-market conditions deteriorate.

observation_candidates.proposition: ABS vacancies fell 0.9 per cent to 325,000 in August 2026; private vacancies fell 2.0 per cent, public vacancies rose 7.8 per cent, and total vacancies were 31.2 per cent below the May 2022 peak.
counter_evidence: Vacancies alone do not establish rising unemployment or recession.
observation_candidates.notes: Prospective transition variable for housing stress.

observation_candidates.proposition: The ABC live blog reported a roughly 2 per cent ASX 200 fall, elevated Australian long-bond yields and stressed oil pricing; these remain contextual market sensors.
counter_evidence: A single session is noisy and the market observations were not independently reconstructed for this packet.
observation_candidates.notes: Context only; cannot independently promote a governed downstream object.

relationship_candidates.title: Global energy shock to Australian inflation and monetary-policy constraint
relationship_candidates.mechanism_candidate: The RBA explicitly linked higher global energy prices and fuel pass-through to its inflation assessment and September tightening decision.
alternative_explanations: Domestic capacity pressure and stronger inflation also contributed.
falsification_conditions: Primary evidence later shows materially weaker energy pass-through or the policy constraint changes as inflation normalises.

relationship_candidates.title: Restrictive financial conditions to housing and household cash-flow compression
relationship_candidates.mechanism_candidate: Candidate chain only; the full chain has not met the production Relationship standard.
alternative_explanations: Housing supply, tax settings, migration, credit standards and household income may alter the path.
falsification_conditions: Housing and household stress stabilise despite continued restrictive conditions.

relationship_candidates.title: Housing weakness to labour and balance-sheet feedback
relationship_candidates.mechanism_candidate: Prospective feedback hypothesis; labour deterioration is the principal transition variable into broad balance-sheet stress.
alternative_explanations: Buffers, income growth, refinancing or policy support may interrupt the feedback.
falsification_conditions: Employment and hours remain resilient while arrears and forced-sale indicators remain contained.

risk_state_candidate.title: Australian monetary-housing compression

stages.label: AFFORDABILITY_AND_MARKET_DETERIORATION
stages.basis: Housing prices and new housing lending have weakened while policy remains restrictive.

stages.label: HOUSEHOLD_CASHFLOW_COMPRESSION
stages.basis: Mortgage cash-flow pressure is visible for a minority while aggregate arrears remain low.

stages.label: BALANCE_SHEET_AND_FORCED_SALE_FEEDBACK
stages.basis: Negative equity is rare and household liquidity buffers remain substantial.

threshold_basis_candidate.description: Stage 3 requires reviewed broad balance-sheet, forced-sale or comparable feedback evidence; falling prices alone are insufficient.

falsification_conditions: Housing and arrears stabilise; labour remains resilient; or inflation pressure recedes enough to relax the policy constraint.

scenario_set_candidate.scope: Australia macro-financial transmission from the 1 October 2026 knowledge cutoff
scenario_set_candidate.shared_starting_condition: Stage 1 active; Stage 2 emerging; Stage 3 not established.

scenario_candidates.title: Controlled adjustment
scenario_candidates.description: Energy and inflation pressure recede, labour remains resilient and housing stabilises before Stage 3 develops.

scenario_candidates.title: Stagflationary squeeze
scenario_candidates.description: External energy inflation constrains monetary relief while housing and interest-sensitive domestic demand weaken.

scenario_candidates.title: Employment-triggered housing feedback
scenario_candidates.description: Labour deterioration weakens debt service, lifting arrears/forced sales and feeding back into housing and demand.

prospective_assessment.statement: Evidence supports active Stage 1 housing deterioration and emerging Stage 2 household cash-flow compression. Stage 3 balance-sheet and forced-sale feedback is not established. Labour-market deterioration is the principal prospective transition variable.
prospective_assessment.hindsight_control: Later evidence may revise the candidate but must not rewrite this as-of interpretation.

known_limitations: Review material only; governed production layers remain unchanged.
ABC market material is context only and is not production-support eligible.
No governed primary-source national housing-price series is added here.
No scenario is ranked, scored or assigned a future-outcome probability.
Risk/Regime and Scenario production gates remain closed.
